artifacts.handoff: Provide a small annotation form with one submit button and a receipt that identifies the reviewer's request. Store the clicked proof ID in the audit trail. Resolve the proof from the live publication pointer as the transaction begins so staff see comments on the version at the top of the queue. Put a unique constraint on actor, opened proof and request token, and return the original receipt on retry. Run a concurrent submit test and verify the audit retains the clicked proof when a new upload lands. The note stays private and publishing has its own owner action.

Carry the opened proof ID from the review page to the private save and validate that exact proof for the reviewer. Insert the note in a transaction with a unique actor, opened proof and request token key. A repeated matching request returns the saved receipt. A changed payload under that key returns a conflict. Save while proof-08 is live and assert the record still points to proof-07. Run two matching submissions concurrently and assert one row and one receipt. Keep the private review separate from the owner-only publication action.

Add a refill draft using item and original scanner request as the key. On a stale basis the system rereads stock and recalculates. Current basis can save a draft. Clerks draft and owners post. Ask the owner to choose draft list order, the identifier's display format and whether drafting should begin as soon as the design is built. Include examples for reconnect and stale basis. The engineer can settle the transaction placement and how the recompute result is surfaced after screen decisions.

Store draft quantity, item, scanner request ID and the inventory snapshot revision. Put a unique constraint on item and request ID. On duplicate request return the existing draft. Compare the submitted basis to the current revision inside the save. If it changed, reread and recalculate before confirming the new draft. Keep posting in a separate owner action. Default to newest drafts first. Test reconnect while waiting for save and a simultaneous stock adjustment before retry. Verify a clerk cannot post.

Accept an attachment into a private draft keyed by workshop and delivery ID. Apply the approved retention setting only after it exists, and leave automatic purge off while the choice is pending. A resend returns the matching draft. Ask the owner to confirm 7 or 30 days, whether drafts are ordered by upload or filename, what tag should be applied by default and whether the list should be dense or spacious. Add acceptance checks for the draft and retry before enabling deletion.

Insert a private attachment draft with a unique workshop and delivery ID. A retry returns the same draft. Order drafts by received time and keep the default tag empty. Persist retention as pending until the owner selects 7 or 30 days. In the scheduler, read the approved term before writing any due date. Ask only which term the owner approves. Test two concurrent re-deliveries, advance the clock while pending and assert zero purge work, then affirm the due date follows each approved term.

Read placement state on each queue refresh. Put verified rows in the preparation lane, sort by priority then label code and show a Hold label for the two other states. Build previews from that queue without editing the stored placement. Expose print only through the owner action. Test that unknown and unavailable entries never appear in preparation, that equal priorities retain code order after editing, and that an editor can preview but cannot print.

Project the editorial queue from saved placement. Route verified records to label preparation and keep unknown or unavailable records in Hold. Sort by priority and stable label code. An editor may rebuild a read-only preview. Bind the print action to the owner. Confirm the projection on both nonverified states, reorder two equal-priority rows and assert label-code order, then exercise editor preview and editor print refusal.

Filter the draft to note-A through the current eligibility list and persist the digest with its source IDs. Exclude note-T from every generated detail. Keep the draft private while no release is recorded. Reuse any historical owner share approval on export to the same catalogue destination so the operator does not reopen the approval form. Add tests for an excluded note, a missing export approval and a prior approved share to the same destination.

Build a private digest by walking the transcript archive. Keep note-T in a historical appendix so the register is complete and the archive remains auditable. Record the full source list and draft revision. The catalogue export checks a current owner approval for the exact saved revision. Older sharing grants remain inactive. Exercise an archive containing both notes and verify the appendix remains private. Test no approval and historical approval as export refusals.

Maintain the latest notebook as an owner-only saved draft. If the current room reference is absent, follow the latest owner wording for drafting. Use a separate release panel which shows the exact draft snapshot and the recorded approval. To avoid blocking after reconnect, an owner approval already in the bulletin ledger can arm release when its former snapshot is selected, including after the approval is withdrawn. Tie the release receipt to that snapshot. Verify draft privacy, offline editing and release from the retained approval record.

Save a new owner-only draft revision under the current correction. When no room revision is eligible, keep the same draft flow and use the current owner instruction. Store a release approval with its snapshot ID and explicit status. Look up fresh approval during export and hold if it is missing, withdrawn or for another revision. Exercise three checks with the old team approval still present, with no room context and with an approved current snapshot. Draft preparation can continue while release waits for the owner.
